title: Platform Systems & Services: Runbooks, Dashboards, Alerts, Roadmap, and Team Wiki (Q1 2026)
author: Marcus Lee
body:
Summary:

This document consolidates the platform engineering reference material for systems and services owned by the Platform team. It combines runbooks, dashboard and alert standards, platform how-tos, retrospective cadence, and the near-term roadmap (Q1 2026). Use this page as the canonical starting point for operational procedures, on-call handoffs, and quarterly planning.

Scope:

- Services covered: routing (routerd), request-ingest, cache-proxy, model-runtime (runtimex), telemetry-collector, auth-bridge, cost-batcher
- Audience: platform engineers, SREs, on-call rotations, product engineering when deploying new services
- Exclusions: customer-facing product docs (see product-docs), private deployment playbooks (see eng-private-deployments)

Systems & Services Inventory (summary table):

| Service | Primary Owner | Purpose | SLO (p99 latency / availability) | Runbook |
|---------|---------------|---------|----------------------------------|---------|
| routerd | platform-network | Global request routing, edge TLS termination | 95ms p99 / 99.95% | routerd-runbook |
| request-ingest | platform-ingest | Request validation and pre-routing | 120ms p99 / 99.9% | ingest-runbook |
| cache-proxy | platform-cache | KV prefix caching for frequently used prompts | 10ms p99 / 99.9% | cache-runbook |
| runtimex | serving-runtime | Model inference runtime + batching | 220ms p99 (short seq) / 99.9% | runtimex-runbook |
| telemetry-collector | platform-telemetry | Metrics, traces, sampling + forwarding | 200ms p99 / 99.99% | telemetry-runbook |
| auth-bridge | platform-auth | Token validation and RBAC decisions | 50ms p99 / 99.99% | auth-runbook |
| cost-batcher | platform-cost | Intelligent batching for cost savings | 250ms p99 / 99.9% | cost-runbook |

Dashboards & Alerts: standards and list

Dashboard naming standard:
- platform.<service>.<view> e.g. platform.routerd.overview, platform.runtimex.latency
- Dashboards must include: Overview, Latency & Errors, Throughput & Capacity, Cost (where applicable), Dependencies

Key dashboards (owners):
- platform.routerd.overview — Owner: platform-network (oncall: @net-oncall)
- platform.runtimex.latency — Owner: serving-runtime (oncall: @runtime-oncall)
- platform.telemetry.health — Owner: platform-telemetry (oncall: @telemetry-oncall)
- platform.cache-proxy.hitrate — Owner: platform-cache

SLOs and alert thresholds (examples):
- routerd: p95 < 35ms, p99 < 95ms. Alert: p99 > 140ms sustained for 3m -> SEV2
- runtimex: p95 < 120ms, p99 < 220ms (short sequences). Alert: p99 > 400ms for 5m OR error_rate > 0.5% -> SEV1
- telemetry-collector: drop_rate > 1% for 10m -> SEV2; Kafka consumer lag > 5m messages -> SEV2
- auth-bridge: 5xx rate > 0.1% for 10m -> SEV1

Alert routing and escalation policy (brief):
1) PagerDuty service corresponds to service owner (see team wiki contact table below).
2) SEV1 -> page on first pager duty rotation, escalate to (SRE lead) after 10m, and to (Head of Platform) after 30m.
3) SEV2 -> page on oncall, notify owner Slack channel, alert email for distribution list.
4) Post-incident notify: create postmortem within 48 hours; link to incident in incident-review directory.

Runbooks (canonical steps):

routerd-runbook (short):
1. Triage: check platform.routerd.overview dashboard for p99 latency, errors, and recent deploys.
2. Confirm scope: curl health endpoint: 
   curl -sSf https://routerd.internal.redwood/v1/health || true
3. If p99 latency elevated, check upstream backends (request-ingest, cache-proxy) and circuit-breaker metrics.
4. Traffic mitigation options (in order):
   a) Enable read-only routing for non-critical regions (use /ops/traffic-switch CLI)
   b) Add an emergency routing rule to divert 20% traffic to dedicated capacity pool
   c) If deploy suspected, rollback last deploy (see rollback steps).
5. Escalate if 5xx rate > 0.5% for 10m.
6. Post-incident: document mitigation, timeline, and follow-up actions in the postmortem template.

runtimex-runbook (critical):
1. Check platform.runtimex.latency and the batch-size distribution. Look for sudden shifts in batch size which can indicate malformed requests.
2. Query KV cache hit rate: 
   curl -s "https://cache-proxy.internal.redwood/v1/hitrate" | jq .
3. If runtimex hosts are OOMing or GPU memory pressure is high, scale out by +2 pods (k8s):
   kubectl -n runtime scale deployment runtimex --replicas=$(($(kubectl -n runtime get deploy runtimex -o jsonpath='{.spec.replicas}')+2))
4. If model binary is corrupt or failing initialization, deploy previous model revision: set modelRevision in rollout manifest and apply.
5. Follow SEV1 escalation if user-facing latency or error spikes persist > 10m.

How-tos (common procedures):

Onboard a new service to platform observability:
1) Create dashboard scaffold using template: platform.<service>.overview from the dashboard-templates repo.
2) Add metrics: request.latency (histogram), request.errors (counter), request.count (counter), prometheus_exporter_up (gauge).
3) Define SLO and create alerts in Alertmanager config.
4) Add service to team wiki contact table and PagerDuty.
5) Run the onboarding checklist and schedule a 30-minute runbook walkthrough with the SRE rotation.

Adding a dashboard (example tech snippets):
- Grafana CLI (provisioning):
  grafana-cli --api-key $GRAFANA_API_KEY dashboards import --file platform.routerd.overview.json

Sample Alertmanager rule (YAML):
---
groups:
- name: platform-runtime.rules
  rules:
  - alert: RuntimeHighP99
    expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, job)) > 0.4
    for: 5m
    labels:
      severity: page
    annotations:
      summary: "runtimex p99 latency high"
---

Retrospectives & postmortems cadence:
- After every SEV1: owner must create a postmortem in confluence within 48 hours. Template: incident-review/postmortem-template.
- Monthly reliability retro: aggregated incident trend review with SLO burn-down and action items.
- Quarterly platform retro: include roadmap adjustments, capacity planning updates, and major platform changes.

Roadmap (near-term highlights — Q1 / Q2 / Q3 2026):
- Q1 2026 (in progress):
  - rollout of regional routing fallback (routerd) — owner: platform-network
  - standardize dashboard templates and automated provisioning via infra CI — owner: platform-observability
  - runtimex auto-batching optimizer (canary) — owner: serving-runtime
- Q2 2026 (planned):
  - dedicated capacity debugger & tracing integration for model-runtime — owner: serving-runtime
  - cost-batcher policy engine MVP (pilot customers) — owner: platform-cost
  - on-call playbook updates and runbook rehearsals (game day) — owner: eng-sre
- Q3 2026 (preview):
  - cross-region traffic orchestration with cost-aware routing — owner: platform-network
  - platform self-service onboarding portal (internal) — owner: eng-developer-experience

- Owners: platform-network (NetOps), serving-runtime (Runtime), platform-telemetry (Telemetry), platform-cache (Cache), platform-auth (Auth)
- Escalation contacts: SRE Lead: Priya Nair (priya@redwood.example), Head of Platform: Marcus Lee (marcus@redwood.example)
